question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can express our integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{x+1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

To evaluate the first integral, we start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & ={x}^{2}+1 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ \text{d}u & =2x\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u & =x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{2}+1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & \sqrt{3} \\ u & 1 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+1)}\,x\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

To evaluate the second integral, we can use the definition of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.$ Finally, we can solve the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{x+1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u+{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u+\operatorname{arctan}⁡x{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{1}^{4}+(\frac{\pi }{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))+\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{2})+\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
